title: You are in or witness a car crash
lede: The noise stops and there is a strange quiet. Glass, a horn stuck on, an engine still running, someone shouting. Your hands are not fully yours yet.

blocks.text: The noise stops and there is a strange quiet. Glass, a horn stuck on, an engine still running, someone shouting. Your hands are not fully yours yet.

items: The second collision is the one that kills responders and survivors — traffic that has not yet realised what is ahead. Scene safety comes before care, always, without exception.
Adrenaline masks your own injuries completely for twenty minutes or more. Feeling fine is not clinical information about your spine or your organs.
What you say in the first minutes gets recorded and used later by insurers and, sometimes, courts. Apologising reflexively can be treated as accepting liability.

items.detail: Hazard lights, engine off, handbrake. Get people off the carriageway and behind a barrier if there is one.

items.move: Call emergency services with a precise location
items.detail: Motorway marker post, junction number, landmark. Say how many vehicles and roughly how many people.

items.move: Do not move injured people unless there is fire or immediate danger
items.detail: Spinal injury is invisible and moving badly can convert a recoverable injury into a permanent one.
Firm direct pressure with whatever fabric is available, and keep it there. This is the one intervention that beats waiting.

items.move: Talk to anyone conscious and trapped
items.detail: Do not leave them alone. Reassurance measurably reduces shock, and you are doing something real by staying.

items.move: Exchange details, factually, without discussing fault
items.detail: Name, insurer, registration, photographs of positions and damage before vehicles move.

items.say: "M4 westbound, just past junction 12, marker 118. Two cars, one on its side. Three people, one not moving."
"I'm staying with you. Help is coming. Don't try to move — just keep looking at me."
"Let's just swap details and let the insurers work out the rest." Never "I'm so sorry, it was my fault."

items: Standing on the carriageway to direct traffic or take photos.
Admitting fault, or arguing it, at the scene.
Declining assessment because you feel fine. Internal bleeding and concussion both present late.
Driving home in shock. Your reaction time is not what you think it is.
Get medically assessed the same day, even without visible injury, and get it documented. Late-presenting injuries with no record are a nightmare to claim for.
Write your own account within 24 hours while sequence memory is intact.
Report to your insurer promptly regardless of fault or intention to claim — late notification voids cover.
Expect intrusive replays and jumpiness in traffic for a week or two. If it persists beyond a month, that is worth treating.

limit: Call emergency services for any injury, any suspected head or neck injury, any unconscious person, any fuel leak or smoke, or any dispute about what happened. Do not move an injured person unless there is fire or oncoming traffic. Never admit liability at the scene; that is for insurers and, if needed, courts to determine.
